title: Preserve JACK routes while configured ports are unavailable
problem: Playing a cue while its configured JACK destination is absent disconnects the current usable route and emits a full traceback, disrupting offline show preparation.
reproduce: Give an output a working fallback connection while its saved destination is absent, then apply the saved route. The pinned baseline disconnects the fallback and attempts the missing destination.
acceptance: An output with any unavailable configured destination retains its current connections and logs one concise warning; once all destinations are available, the saved route replaces the current connections.
repair: Reconcile JACK connections per output after enumerating available input ports, skip destructive changes for incomplete target sets, and log expected JACK errors without exception tracebacks.

verification.limitations: BCL exercises route reconciliation and JACK failures with deterministic doubles. A live JACK graph and hot-unplugged client remain owner-validated.
verification.ownerCheck: Connect a cue to an external JACK client, remove that client, play and save the session, then reconnect the client and reopen/play the session. Confirm no traceback, the temporary live route is retained while absent, and the saved route returns when available.

selection.reason: A fresh external report gives exact JACK hot-unplug steps and a clear preservation requirement; deterministic route tests reproduce the destructive baseline without requiring the physical interface.
